chapter: Early New Orleans bands and records
title: Personnel of the Brownlee band
summary: The spot-job band, with Harry Shields, Joe Loyacano, the banjo player and drummer Alonzo Crumby.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Joe Lloyd Canner. Do you remember who else was in the band? Yeah. I may have made a note of some of the people who were on the record, but I was wondering about where did you work with the band?

Well it was what they call a spot job band. In other words they'd play, maybe tonight they'd play Over the River, and the next night they'd play here, West Wego, all around us. What they call a spot job band here. Yeah.
Casual engagements. Harry Shields was on that record. Harry Shields played.

Did he play with you much in those days? Yes. Yes. Mostly. Harry mostly played the clarinet with me all the time. There was Harry Shields, Brown Lee, Joe Lloyd Canner, myself, and I can't think of his name, but it was Brown Lee's brother-in-law that played the banjo.
Oh I have a note on the record, it was French, Barrowman French. That's his name, yeah.
And Crum, I think it was something like that. I just can't remember.

Yeah, a drummer, Alonzo Crumby. Alonzo Crumby, right. I was going to ask about Harry Shields. I never got to hear his brother, older brother. Do you think their styles are a good deal the same? I like Harry's playing very much and it sounds to me somewhat... The sounds are practically the same.
